reviews: My sister has a serious peanut allergy and avoids most Thai places, but this one is her Friday ritual. She's been ordering something different every week for a year, curries and dipping sauces included, and has never had a single reaction. Right now it's the pad see ew with extra Chinese broccoli, always at the table under the hanging orchids.

Steamed fish with lime and chili, stir-fried morning glory and a clear lemongrass soup. The line runs out the door at noon, so come a bit early. I walked back to my desk feeling fresh instead of sleepy, with change left over from a ten.
The satay is the reason to come: grilled skewers with a thick peanut dip on the side, and they shower the noodles and the salads with crushed peanuts too. You can smell it from the sidewalk.
Grilled chicken, bright herb salads and a broth that tastes clean, nothing swimming in oil. A smart pick when you still have a 2pm meeting to stay awake through.

I'm allergic to peanuts, so Thai food is usually a minefield of surprise toppings and sauces for me. Here I've eaten my way through most of the menu, sauces and all, without so much as an itch. Look for the carved wooden door at the end of the alley; there's no sign.

Nearly everything comes out of the fryer or a very well-oiled wok: crispy pork belly, battered wings, a pad see ew glistening with oil, spring rolls leaving grease spots on the paper. Tasty, but I spent the whole afternoon feeling like I'd swallowed a brick.

Booked the back room overlooking the river for our team lead's farewell lunch. I called ahead about her peanut allergy, and the woman on the phone said she could order anything she liked because peanuts never come through their kitchen door. A lovely send-off, but the bill was a step up from our usual intern lunch.
Herb salad, steamed sea bass, a pad see ew with more greens than noodles and a tom yum so clear you can see the bottom of the bowl. I stayed sharp right through the afternoon slump.

Still my favorite light lunch on the block: a few cucumber rolls, salmon nigiri and a cup of miso, and I'm back at my desk feeling great instead of stuffed. Grab one of the eight stools and watch the chef slice.

Nothing but sushi here, served with soy, pickled ginger and wasabi, and that's it: no sesame-peanut dressings, no crunchy nut toppings like at some counters nearby. Our manager can't have peanuts, so whenever she picks the team lunch it's this place, and she's never had a scare.
